title: Experiment signal decomposition and metric ownership playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket captures a playbook for decomposing experiment signals (A/B tests, staged rollouts, and lightweight canaries) across product, model, and infra layers and assigning clear metric ownership. The goal is to reduce noisy experiment readouts, accelerate decision-making during rollouts, and ensure fast, accountable escalations when quality or latency regressions surface. Scope includes: a signal taxonomy, ownership matrix, dashboard checklists, instrumentation requirements, milestone gating criteria, and an escalation ladder for automated and manual rollbacks. Deliverables: a canonical Confluence signal taxonomy page, a set of Grafana dashboards + alert recipes, a metric ownership registry in the Experiment Catalog, and a short training doc for PMs/Eng/MLOps.
milestones: M1: Draft signal taxonomy and ownership matrix (2025-01-20)
M2: Instrumentation spec + required attributes for telemetry events (2025-01-30)
M3: Dashboard templates and alert thresholds implemented in staging (2025-02-10)
M4: Pilot the playbook on current runtime batching experiment (2025-02-18)
M5: Post-pilot retro and finalize runbook for inclusion in Experimentation framework (2025-02-28)
acceptance_criteria: Signal taxonomy documented with at least three concrete examples per category (user, request, model, infra)
Metric ownership registry created with named owner and on-call fallback for each primary metric
Dashboards are available in staging and reflect all required breakdowns (by model-version, route, region, and customer tier)
Automated alerts for high-priority regressions (latency > SLO, correctness delta > threshold) are configured and tested
Runbook describes step-by-step escalation and rollback triggers and is approved by Eng, SRE, and ML teams
instrumentation_requirements: Add model-version tag and route_id to all generation telemetry events
Surface KV-cache hit ratio and per-request cache latency in traces
Emit an experiment_id and cohort tag for every request during an experiment window
Record end-to-end p95/p99 latency split by inference-time and network time
Create a lightweight quality signal: prompt+response hash histogram to track abnormal deltas over baseline
runbook_summary: When a signal breach is detected, follow: 1) Triage using dashboard playbook (owner verifies metric and scope), 2) If regression isolated to a single model-version or region, trigger automated rollback to previous stable variant, 3) If regression spans routes or capacity tiers, engage SRE and ML leads and escalate to on-call product manager. Use experiment_id to reconstruct request traces and attach a postmortem to the experiment entry in the Experiment Catalog.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overlap of metrics across experiments causing confounded signals -> Mitigation: enforce experiment_id and cohort tagging and isolate traffic partitions where feasible
Risk: Alert fatigue from low-signal thresholds -> Mitigation: provide templated threshold suggestions tuned by historical variance and allow temporary snoozes during low-risk windows
Risk: Ownership ambiguity between PM and ML engineer for quality metrics -> Mitigation: ownership matrix requires a named owner and a documented fallback contact before experiment approval
